title: Reading AI Papers Without Getting Lost

sections.subtitle: Read the abstract last
sections.description:
The abstract tells you the claim. The method tells you how the claim was tested. Read the method and experiments before deciding whether the abstract is convincing.

A useful order: figures, method, experiments, limitations, then abstract.

visualization.title: Paper anatomy
visualization.html:
Paper anatomy

Title
Abstract — the claim
Introduction — why it matters
Method — how it works
Experiments — evidence
Limitations — what is not covered

sections.subtitle: Reproduce one number
sections.description:
Pick a single result from the paper and try to reproduce it, even approximately. This exposes hidden assumptions faster than reading the appendix.

If you cannot reproduce it, write down exactly which piece is missing.

sections.subtitle: Keep a claim-evidence table
sections.description:
For each claim, record the evidence, the dataset, and the baseline. This turns a pile of papers into a map of what is actually known.

Claims without evidence are hypotheses. Treat them that way.
